title: Breakpoints and step debugging
learningObjectives: Explain breakpoints and step debugging and debug or organise JavaScript code using the concept.

understand.concept: A breakpoint pauses JavaScript execution at a chosen line so a developer can inspect variables and control flow. Step over executes the current line without entering called functions; step into enters a function; step out runs until the current function returns. Watch expressions and call stacks provide additional context.
understand.whyItMatters: Step debugging reveals how values change and which branch executes. It is more reliable than adding many console logs when investigating complex state.
understand.analogy: A breakpoint is a pause point in a journey; stepping lets you inspect each next action.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; debugger, module, prototype, and function-call behaviour follow JavaScript and browser runtime rules.

explain.narrative: Set a breakpoint inside calculate and inspect price, quantity, subtotal, and tax as execution proceeds.

examples.explanation: Set a breakpoint inside calculate and inspect price, quantity, subtotal, and tax as execution proceeds.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page demonstrates the code organisation or runtime behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Use browser developer tools to pause inside a function. Step over, step into, and step out while watching a variable change.
practise.independentTask: Create a small example that uses the feature. Inspect its runtime behaviour and explain the scope, receiver, or call path involved.
hints: Use breakpoints to inspect changing values.
Test methods both through their object and when passed as callbacks.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Breakpoints and step debugging</title></head><body>
<script>function calculate(price,quantity){const subtotal=price*quantity;const tax=subtotal*.18;return subtotal+tax;}console.log(calculate(100,2));</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which debugger action executes the current line without entering a called function?
questions.explanation: Step over executes the current statement and pauses at the next one.

questions.prompt: What is a useful debugging or architecture practice?
options: Inspect actual runtime behaviour and keep dependencies explicit
Assume the code behaves as intended
questions.answer: Inspect actual runtime behaviour and keep dependencies explicit
questions.explanation: Reliable debugging and modular design depend on understanding actual execution and dependencies.
